alternatives.why_not_first: Usability has the second-highest baseline severity sum ({A05}), led by excessive ad interruptions ({C10}) and playlist/queue misbehavior ({C18}), and its complaint share held roughly flat between periods ({T18}); it also leads on raw complaint count in both label sets, but the baseline metric still places it behind billing/support ({A02} versus {A05}).

Playback/performance has a lower baseline severity sum ({A08}) than billing/support, led by unexpected stops/skips ({C14}) and crashes ({C22}), and its share of reviews declined between the compared periods ({T15}); the verifier's sample does rank it first on severity ({T46}), which is a reason to watch it but not yet to override the larger-sample baseline order.

Access/onboarding has by far the smallest baseline severity sum ({A17}), driven by login failures ({C30}), and even though its share of reviews grew ({T09}), it remains the smallest area by complaint share ({T28}, range {T29} to {T30}).

limitations: The verifier's labels disagree with the enricher's labels on which area ranks first by severity sum ({T42} versus {T46}), so the billing/support lead should be treated as provisional pending a larger verified sample.

The premium_only issue ({C02}) reflects packaging and policy objections rather than technical billing defects, so standard 'billing/support' remediation playbooks (refunds, payment fixes) will not address it.
Period and spike-month comparisons ({T01}, {T02}, {T31}, {T35}) describe shifting review volume and mix, not a controlled measurement of underlying issue frequency.
next_quarter_actions: Pilot clearer in-app messaging and staged rollout of free-tier limits tied to the Premium-only restrictions issue ({C02}), testing whether complaint count ({C01}) or severity sum ({C02}) for that issue declines.

Review whether specific free-tier controls (skip limits, forced shuffle, repeat/rewind) can be partially restored or better explained, aiming to reduce the area's share of complaints ({A03}) in the next period comparison.

As a hedge, prioritize a scoped investigation into playback stability (stops/skips {C14}, crashes {C22}) given the verifier's alternate ranking ({T46}), tracking whether its severity sum narrows the gap with billing/support in a future verified sample.
Monitor the trend share for billing/support ({T12}) into the next comparable period to confirm it continues rising rather than reversing.
rationale: Billing/support's baseline severity sum ({A02}) exceeds usability ({A05}), playback/performance ({A08}) and access/onboarding ({A17}), and is dominated by the single premium_only issue ({C02}) with a high mean severity ({C03}).
The area's share of reviews grew from {T10} in {T01} to {T11} in {T02}, a change of {T12}, the largest increase of any area in that comparison, while playback/performance's share fell ({T15}).
A spike month ({T35}) shows the premium_only issue rising sharply ({T38}) relative to other months, consistent with the area's growth pattern.

Within sampling intervals, billing/support's complaint share ({T22}, range {T23} to {T24}) is close to usability's ({T19}, range {T20} to {T21}), so the lead over usability is not wide, though it still exceeds playback/performance's complaint share ({T25}).

The independent verifier's labels do not fully agree: on the same severity-sum metric the verifier ranks playback/performance first in its sample ({T46}) and billing/support third ({T48}), whereas the enricher labels rank billing/support first ({T42}) and playback/performance third ({T44}); both label sets agree usability leads on complaint count alone.
output.recommendation: Billing/support carries the highest baseline priority ({A02}), driven almost entirely by the Premium-only restrictions issue ({C02}, mean severity {C03} across {C01} complaint and cancellation reviews). This issue is a free-tier packaging and entitlement policy question - what the free tier includes (skip limits, forced shuffle, inability to pick, repeat or rewind songs) and how changes to it are rolled out and explained - not a payment, checkout or support-backlog defect.
what_would_change_the_call: If a larger verified sample confirms the verifier's ordering with playback/performance ahead of billing/support on severity sum ({T46} versus {T48}), that would weaken the recommendation.
If billing/support's share of reviews reverses and falls back toward its earlier-period level ({T10}) in the same months of the following year, that would weaken the case for prioritizing it.
If the spike-month lift in premium_only complaints ({T38} in {T35}) fades back to the level seen in other months, that would suggest the issue is less persistent than the baseline priority implies.

payload.decision_rule: baseline priority = severity_sum over complaint and cancellation reviews; areas sum their issues

payload.question: Where should the next quarter of product-improvement effort go: access/onboarding, usability, playback/performance, or billing/support?

top_issues.definition: Features locked to Premium: skip limits, forced shuffle, cannot pick songs, cannot repeat or rewind, lyrics or offline behind a paywall, 'everything needs Premium now'.
top_issues.name: Premium-only restrictions
top_issues.summary: Customers report that core playback features like song selection, skipping, repeat, and full-song playback are locked behind a Premium paywall.

top_issues.definition: General praise or criticism with no specific feature, unrelated content (politics, artists, boycotts), or meaningless text.
top_issues.name: General or unrelated

top_issues.definition: Too many, too long, too loud or repeated ads; ads interrupting listening.
top_issues.name: Excessive ad interruptions
top_issues.summary: Customers report that frequent, repeated ads interrupt music and podcast listening, causing irritation and frustration with the app.

top_issues.definition: Music stops, pauses, skips by itself, will not start, or plays the wrong song.
top_issues.name: Playback stops or skips unexpectedly
top_issues.summary: Customers report that playback randomly pauses, stops, fails to start, or plays the wrong track, disrupting their listening experience.

top_issues.definition: Managing the queue, playlists, liked songs or library; shuffle or repeat controls that misbehave.
top_issues.name: Playlist and queue playback misbehaving
top_issues.summary: Customers report that playlists, queues, and shuffle/repeat controls play unexpected or wrong songs, disrupt saved order, or fail to respect user edits.

top_issues.definition: App crashes, freezes, will not open or load, blank screens.
top_issues.name: App crashes and fails to load
top_issues.summary: Customers report the app freezes, crashes, or gets stuck on the loading logo, preventing them from using it after updates or reinstalls.

top_issues.definition: Hard to find things, confusing layout, redesigns or home-screen changes, buttons moved or removed.
top_issues.name: Confusing redesigned home screen layout
top_issues.summary: Customers report that recent redesigns made the home screen and interface cluttered, less user-friendly, and harder to navigate to familiar content.

top_issues.definition: Cannot log in, keeps getting logged out, login or verification-code errors.
top_issues.name: Login failures
top_issues.summary: Customers are unable to log in or verify their account due to missing codes, phone number errors, or being repeatedly logged out, disrupting app access.

top_issues.definition: Notifications, emails, settings, toggles, widgets and other interaction annoyances.
top_issues.name: Other control annoyances

top_issues.definition: Recommendations, the algorithm, autoplay or radio picks, the DJ, unwanted suggested songs.
top_issues.name: Unwanted repetitive or forced recommendations
top_issues.summary: Customers report that autoplay, radio, and algorithmic suggestions repeat songs or insert unwanted tracks into playlists, disrupting their intended listening experience.

period_comparison.method: share = complaint/cancellation reviews in the area / all classified reviews in the period; Wilson 95% intervals; identical calendar months one year apart avoid the partial first/last months and seasonal mix. Descriptive only: reviews are self-selected, not a customer census.

verifier_robustness.metric: severity_sum (the baseline priority) over complaint and cancellation reviews, row-weighted
